a inf-unbounded bound must mean the same thing to all four readers. ROUND-6 (F3, the A05 vacuity class): the obs carries a NAN cell deliberately. Over the old finite obs the range a reader would build if it DID accept '-inf'/'inf' is [-inf, inf], which admits every finite value — so the case answered all-true whether the bound was rejected or honoured, and could not fail. A nan cell fails `-inf <= x <= inf` in every reader, so honouring the bound now shows up as a dropped cell

a Infinity-unbounded bound must mean the same thing to all four readers. ROUND-6 (F3, the A05 vacuity class): the NAN cell is what makes this case able to fail — see A08; over finite cells a reader that accepted 'Infinity' built [-inf, inf] and answered exactly the all-true mask a reader that rejected it does

R3-81: the numeric fallback deliberately matches every DECIMAL spelling of the kept value ('01', ' 1', '+1', '1.0', '1e0'). That is wider than a literal string compare, and it is the fix for the dtype divergence (a float column spells its 1 as '1.0'), so all four readers must widen IDENTICALLY — pinned here in both directions
…and the fallback does NOT widen to spellings outside the ONE grammar

JS String(1e-7) is '1e-7' where python str(1e-07) is '1e-07' — the numeric fallback is what makes that spelling difference invisible to the mask; pinned so a future 'simplification' of the fallback surfaces here

R3-112 (mask side): a keep-set on an ABSENT column imposes NO constraint in all three mask readers — the DSL builder lifting it into a real constraint is the divergence, and it is recorded here as the mask's answer

R4A-01: serde spells ["a"] with double quotes, python's str() with single ('[\'a\']') — unspellable
R4A-01: serde spells [true], python's str() spells '[True]' — unspellable
R4A-01: serde spells [null], python's str() spells '[None]' — unspellable
R4A-02: python's str([1.0]) is '[1.0]' and JS CANNOT distinguish 1 from 1.0 — the reason reproducing CPython's repr is unwinnable and the value is refused instead

the CELL-side gate, on its own: a keep value that is LITERALLY python's spelling of a container must still not match the container cell — only the real string cell
an unspellable member is dropped from the keep-set, it does not poison the SCALAR members beside it

the KEEP-side gate, on its own: an object keep value matches nothing — not even a string cell that happens to hold python's spelling of it
an EMPTY criteria list constrains nothing — every cell kept, and the emitter refuses to record an all-true 'selection'

a keep-set compares the cell as SPELLED -- no reader trims an obs CELL on the keep path, so a space-padded ' A' does not match the keep value 'A' (and the numeric fallback cannot rescue a non-decimal). The keep path had NO padded-cell case at all: trimming the cell inside the shared `categoricalMatches` diverged from the kernel and the emitted replay on every padded categorical value, at rc 0

…and the canonical shape, a NBSP-padded "\u00a01" (what a spreadsheet / CJK-IME paste yields) against the keep value '1': every reader REFUSES a non-ascii string numerically (`parseBound` / `_bound_or_none` / `_decimal` all gate on ascii), so there is no numeric fallback and the cell does not match. A unicode-aware trim on either side of the comparison flips exactly this cell

a non-finite cell is dropped by a ONE-SIDED bound too. E03 is two-sided, so its comparisons already reject +Inf and the kernel's sole `m &= np.isfinite(vals)` was uncovered: delete it and `+Inf >= 0` keeps this cell while the preview, the emitted replay and the evaluated predicate all drop it

a criterion column SHORTER than the obs length pads KEPT -- deliberately, in all three mask readers (`keep_and`'s missing entry and `keep_mask`'s tail pad, the kernel's `np.concatenate([m, ones])`, the prelude's `i >= len(col)`). Nothing pinned it: 'a' is 2 long and 'b' 3 while the obs is 4, so index 2 exercises the missing-entry rule and index 3 the tail pad
